newsitem.title: USA: Gateway to push for business sector growth.
newsitem.headline: Gateway to push for business sector growth.

text.p: Gateway 2000 Inc, a direct marketer of personal computers, said it will introduce on Wednesday a new line of business computers and detail its plans to increase its share of the corporate PC sales market.
A Gateway spokesman declined to detail the company's plans.
But analysts said the North Sioux City, S.D.-based company is set to introduce new products, including a low-cost network PC, and to announce a beefed up sales force.

Analysts said that the corporate push is a smart move for the company, which is already the leader in direct sales to consumers. They noted that Gateway currently has about six percent of the $38 billion a year corporate market.

Analysts said Gateway's move will result in greater brand identity, but is not likely to take a huge bite of the corporate market, where Compaq Computer Corp, Dell Computer Corp, International Business Machines Corp and Hewlett-Packard Co are the leaders.
"I don't think that anyone is expecting them to come in and gain share hand over fist over the entrenched players," said Louis Mazzucchelli, an analyst at Gerard Klauer Mattison.

"I think Gateway's plan is to come into the business sector small and work their way up," said Richard Schutte of Goldman Sachs. "This is an incremental growth opportunity with the potential for greater global sales."

"It's a smart move," Mazzucchelli said. "They are already in the (corporate) market and they understand the notion of building a brand. They should be able to translate that into the corporate space."

Analysts noted that while Gateway may make a big noise with its new campaign, its gains will probably come from quietly selling to small and mid-sized companies, rather than angling for the larger firms right away.

Some analysts, like Wendy Abromowitz of Argus Research, said Gateway will be able to compete in the long term as long as they make price and value-added items like customer support their major concerns.
